---
title: "17. Seasonal forcing in an open population: R_t around the endemic attractor"
subtitle: "ReproductiveNumbers.jl vignettes"
author: "Simon D. W. Frost"
date: today
---

## Overview

In a closed population a single epidemic burns through the susceptibles and `R_t` falls
below one for good. With births and deaths the susceptible pool is replenished, the
infection persists, and a seasonally varying transmission rate `β(t)` drives recurrent
epidemics on an endemic attractor. There `R_t` oscillates *around one*: the phases in which
`R_t > 1` are the growing parts of each seasonal epidemic and the phases with `R_t < 1` the
declining parts, while the annual average is close to one because susceptibles are
consumed and replaced at the same long-run rate.

The model and parameter values follow the forced SIR chapter of the
[Epidemiological Recipes cookbook](https://epirecip.es/epicookbook/chapters/sirforced/r):
a 70-year life expectancy, a one-week infectious period, an annual sinusoidal forcing of
amplitude 5 %, and a population of 100 000. Time is measured in days.

There is no infection-free *steady* state when `β` varies in time, so `R₀` of the forced
model is not defined through this package's construction (seasonally forced models have
their own `R₀`, defined through a linear operator on periodic functions, Bacaër and
Guernaoui 2006). The effective reproduction number is defined at every instant.

## The model

```{julia}
using ReproductiveNumbers, ModelingToolkit, Symbolics, OrdinaryDiffEqTsit5, Plots, Statistics
using ModelingToolkit: t_nounits as t, D_nounits as D

@parameters β₀ β₁ ω γ μ N
@variables S(t) I(t) R(t)
β = β₀ * (1 + β₁ * sin(ω * t))
sir = complete(System([D(S) ~ μ * N - β * S * I / N - μ * S,
                       D(I) ~ β * S * I / N - (γ + μ) * I,
                       D(R) ~ γ * I - μ * R], t; name = :forced_sir))
```

For reference, the unforced model (`β₁ = 0`) has a unique infection-free steady state and

```{julia}
unforced = complete(System([D(S) ~ μ * N - β₀ * S * I / N - μ * S,
                            D(I) ~ β₀ * S * I / N - (γ + μ) * I,
                            D(R) ~ γ * I - μ * R], t; name = :sir))
R0 = basic_reproduction_number(unforced, [I])
```

```{julia}
p = [β₀ => 10 / 7, β₁ => 0.05, ω => 2π / 365, γ => 1 / 7, μ => 1 / (70 * 365), N => 1e5]
ReproductiveNumbers.to_number(substitute(R0, Dict(p)))
```

## R_t as a function of time and state

```{julia}
Rt = effective_reproduction_number(sir, [I])
```

`R_t` is the product of the seasonal factor and the susceptible fraction, scaled by the
mean infectious period. We add it to the system as an observed variable, spin the model up
for 100 years to reach the attractor, and then follow it for ten years at daily resolution.

```{julia}
sir_Rt, Rtvar = add_effective_reproduction_number(sir, [I])
u0 = [S => 99_999.0, I => 1.0, R => 0.0]
year = 365.0
spinup = solve(ODEProblem(sir_Rt, [u0; p], (0.0, 100year)), Tsit5(); save_everystep = false)
# the state on the attractor, by name (compiled systems may order unknowns differently)
attractor = [S => spinup[S][end], I => spinup[I][end], R => spinup[R][end]]
sol = solve(ODEProblem(sir_Rt, [attractor; p], (0.0, 10year)), Tsit5(); saveat = 1.0)
years = sol.t ./ year
plt = plot(years, sol[I]; label = "I(t)", xlabel = "year", ylabel = "infectious", legend = :topright)
```

```{julia}
plt2 = plot(years, sol[Rtvar]; label = "R_t", xlabel = "year", ylabel = "R_t", legend = :topright)
hline!(plt2, [1.0]; label = "threshold", linestyle = :dash)
```

## Reading the two curves together

`R_t` leads prevalence: infections grow exactly while `R_t > 1` and peak when `R_t`
crosses one from above. Its annual mean is close to one, which is what an endemic
attractor means:

```{julia}
(mean = mean(sol[Rtvar]), minimum = minimum(sol[Rtvar]), maximum = maximum(sol[Rtvar]))
```

The fraction of the population susceptible hovers around `1/R₀`, the endemic level of the
unforced model:

```{julia}
(mean(sol[S]) / 1e5, 1 / ReproductiveNumbers.to_number(substitute(R0, Dict(p))))
```

The seasonal factor `β(t)/β₀` and the susceptible fraction pull in opposite directions
through the year, which is why the amplitude of `R_t` is smaller than the 5 % forcing would
suggest at a fixed susceptible pool:

```{julia}
seasonal = [1 + 0.05 * sin(2π * τ / 365) for τ in sol.t]
plot(years, seasonal; label = "β(t)/β₀", xlabel = "year")
plot!(years, sol[S] ./ mean(sol[S]); label = "S(t)/mean S")
plot!(years, sol[Rtvar]; label = "R_t")
```

## An intervention on the attractor

A control measure that reduces transmission by half for one year, switched on and off
smoothly, pushes `R_t` below one for its duration. Susceptibles accumulate meanwhile, so
when it is lifted `R_t` overshoots and a larger-than-usual epidemic follows.

```{julia}
@parameters c t₁ t₂ k
switch(τ) = 1 / (1 + exp(-k * (τ - t₁))) * (1 - 1 / (1 + exp(-k * (τ - t₂))))
β_int = β * (1 - c * switch(t))
sir_int = complete(System([D(S) ~ μ * N - β_int * S * I / N - μ * S,
                           D(I) ~ β_int * S * I / N - (γ + μ) * I,
                           D(R) ~ γ * I - μ * R], t; name = :forced_sir_intervention))
sir_int_Rt, Rtvar_int = add_effective_reproduction_number(sir_int, [I])
p_int = [p; c => 0.5; t₁ => 2year; t₂ => 3year; k => 0.1]
sol_int = solve(ODEProblem(sir_int_Rt, [attractor; p_int], (0.0, 10year)), Tsit5(); saveat = 1.0)
plt3 = plot(years, sol[Rtvar]; label = "R_t, no intervention", xlabel = "year", ylabel = "R_t")
plot!(plt3, years, sol_int[Rtvar_int]; label = "R_t, intervention in year 2-3")
hline!(plt3, [1.0]; label = "threshold", linestyle = :dash)
```

```{julia}
plot(years, sol[I]; label = "no intervention", xlabel = "year", ylabel = "infectious")
plot!(years, sol_int[I]; label = "intervention in year 2-3")
```

## Evaluating along any solution

The same `R_t` trajectory can be computed from a solution of the original system, without
the observed variable, by evaluating the numeric next-generation matrix at each saved
state (this also works when no closed form exists):

```{julia}
ngm = next_generation_matrix(sir, [I]; equilibrium = Dict(), autonomous = false)
sol0 = solve(ODEProblem(sir, [attractor; p], (0.0, 10year)), Tsit5(); saveat = year / 4)
Rt0 = effective_reproduction_number(ngm, sol0)
maximum(abs, Rt0 .- sol(sol0.t; idxs = Rtvar).u)
```
